summary: Enterprise Suite AC-07 OpenAPI 3.2.0 preview contract for policy, group rollup, Workflow, incident rollback, and ops metadata endpoints.

findings: The contract adds one preview OpenAPI artifact plus semver metadata and keeps runtime behavior out of scope.
Schemas directly reflect DTO crate request names rather than inventing a parallel model.
Explicit preview non-claims prevent accidental production-readiness claims while making API shape reviewable.
Endpoint grouping follows command-style metadata seams for policy, rollup, workflow, incident, and ops integration.

F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Validation fails if the contract stops parsing or loses required semver metadata.
findings: OpenAPI artifact parses as JSON with openapi 3.2.0 and api-semver accepts one contract plus one metadata record.
Integrator-facing paths and operationIds map one-to-one to Enterprise Suite DTO/domain/app seams.
x-oyatie-app-function markers tell later adapter authors which Rust functions the contracts correspond to.
cargo fmt check, API DTO tests, OpenAPI parse, api-semver, dependency-seam, and quality-marker scan passed locally.
No Rust code, dependencies, lockfile, storage adapter, or runtime adapter was added in this slice.

alternatives_named: wait for HTTP runtime before documenting OpenAPI
generate OpenAPI from code later only
write preview OpenAPI aligned to DTO tests now
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: Preview OpenAPI gives integrators and later adapter authors a contract to review while the DTO crate is fresh and tested.
rejected_reasons: Waiting for runtime encourages implementation-led wire shapes.
Generation tooling is not present for these DTO crates and would be a separate slice.

findings: Schemas declare bearer security shape and tenant/evidence/idempotency fields, but do not claim runtime enforcement.
No credential fields or raw secret material are introduced.

F8_performance.regression_baseline: No runtime code path exists; artifact parse and api-semver validation are static checks.

findings.summary: Contract-only slice has no request-time performance footprint.

findings: Schemas carry x-data-class annotations on key tenant/evidence/financial fields.
The contract declares non-claims for auth enforcement, storage, Workflow execution, incident runtime, OpenTofu execution, and cloud integration.
The change is additive contract metadata and can be reverted without data migration, runtime rollback, or external resource teardown.
OpenAPI schemas carry audit/evidence ref fields for future adapters; no logs, metrics, traces, or audit events are emitted by this artifact.
Audit-chain rows record local evidence and Oya VCS closeout.
Enterprise Suite specs now list OpenAPI preview contract rows after DTO contract foundation.

M1_challenge_assumption.premise_stated: A preview OpenAPI artifact is valuable before runtime only if it is explicit about non-deployment and stays aligned to DTO tests.
M1_challenge_assumption.premise_evidence_ref: existing HR/payroll/accounting OpenAPI contracts and oya-enterprise-suite-api tests/contracts.rs
M1_challenge_assumption.do_nothing_consequence: Enterprise Suite would have DTOs but no cross-language wire-shape artifact for integrators or later gateway adapters.
M1_challenge_assumption.upstream_fix_rejection_reason: Runtime adapters are separate and should consume, not define, the wire-shape contract.

findings: This slice completes the first API-first loop for Enterprise Suite: domain/app invariants, API DTOs, then preview OpenAPI contract.
Paths, operationIds, and schema names use Enterprise Suite DTO/domain vocabulary and existing service contract conventions.
Plan, todo, and spec AC-07 document the contract-only surface and verification command.
Contract files live under microservices/enterprise-suite/contracts like HR/payroll/accounting.
No deployed HTTP endpoint, auth middleware, storage adapter, Workflow runtime, incident runtime, OpenTofu runner, or cloud adapter was introduced.
The slice adds no code dependencies.
OpenAPI 3.2.0 document and semver metadata validate through api-semver.
Static schemas use explicit refs, enums, patterns, and required fields rather than dynamic or undocumented request shapes.
